summary: Prevent portaled controls from falling behind project and modal surfaces, and reduce first-screen and route-transition latency.

notes: Authenticated startup identity, platform role, permissions, department, and sidebar order are returned by one security-definer RPC.
The bootstrap function remains unavailable to anon and selects the highest configured platform role when legacy multi-role data exists.
Select menus inherit a semantic dropdown or modal-popover layer from their containing surface.
The desktop project editor no longer creates a modal stacking context; mobile project selects remain above the modal editor.
Authenticated startup uses one RPC with a short token-keyed cache instead of eight requests across three serial waves.
Accessible routes preload during browser idle time, navigation uses real links, and React and TanStack vendors are split into stable cacheable chunks.
Production Nginx compresses JavaScript, CSS, JSON, manifests, XML, SVG, and text responses with gzip.
The sidebar logo is reduced from a 583 KB source PNG to a 13 KB display-sized WebP with fixed dimensions and deferred decoding.
Large project and organization directories use content visibility to reduce off-screen rendering work.

verification: Run npm --prefix frontend run build with VITE_APP_VERSION=V0.19.4.
Run the mocked desktop and mobile project select elementFromPoint Playwright regression.
Back up PostgreSQL, the application directory, and production.env before applying migration 143.
Run scripts/assert-current-user-bootstrap.sql in its rollback transaction.
Run scripts/assert-function-grants.sql and deploy/scripts/pre-deploy-check.sh with EXPECTED_VERSION=V0.19.4.
Run scripts/smoke-frontend-render.mjs and scripts/audit-frontend-performance.mjs against https://xpjs.asia.
Confirm hashed assets return Content-Encoding gzip and immutable cache headers.
